title: Bad specification conditions
statement: Let $C,c$ be natural numbers, let $V$ be a language of Boolean words, and let $x,U,u,j,p$ be Boolean words. The bad-specification condition requires that $|u|=C(|x|+1)^c$, $|j|\le C(|x|+1)^c$, and $|p|\le C(|x|+1)^c$, together with at least one of the following: the query on the encoding of $x,u$ with the word obtained by dropping the marker from $U$ and using a block of $C(|x|+1)^c$ true bits followed by false fails; or $|p|=C(|x|+1)^c$, that query with false prepended to $p$ holds, and the encoding of the pair $(x,u)$ with $p$ is not in $V$; or $|j|+|p|+1=C(|x|+1)^c$, the query with $|j|$ true bits followed by true, false, and then $p$ holds, while the queries with $|j|$ true bits followed by false and then $p$ with either false or true appended both fail.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is a language of Boolean words
At least one of the three stated alternatives holds
caveat: The exact meanings of the query predicate, pair encoding, marker removal, and language $\mathrm{CVAL}$ are not defined in the supplied snippet.
